description: A grand staircase foyer with applied panel wainscoting in crisp white paint covering the stair wall and the flanking side wall. The staircase itself features dark walnut-stained treads with white-painted risers, white-painted turned balusters, and a continuous walnut handrail that curves elegantly up and over a substantial newel post at the base. The paneled walls extend from floor to ceiling with raised rectangular molding panels in a formal, symmetrical grid — a hallmark of traditional American millwork. Warm amber light radiates outward from two positions on the stair wall, casting golden pools across the white paneling and lending honeyed warmth to the pale cream upper walls. In the lower right corner, a small round walnut side table holds a clear glass vase of fresh white calla lilies, their stems and broad green leaves adding a single elegant organic note to the architectural formality. The upper wall above the wainscoting is painted a pale greige-cream, and natural light washes in from an unseen window at the upper landing, brightening the stair passage. Camera is positioned at standing eye-level, three-quarter view of the stair corner where the stair wall meets the adjacent entry wall, shooting upward at a slight angle so both the ascending stairs and the paneled wall to the left are equally visible in frame. The overall mood is formal yet inviting, the rich walnut wood tones warming the crisp white millwork.
